headline: First per-step measurement with the text encoder LIVE on the official undistilled model at the goal's baseline request: 2169.11 s wall, 124 aligned frames, ~33.45 s/step steady state and 34.63 s/it across the 49-step loop - about 2.3x the DiT-only figure. The visible artefact reproduces with the live encoder and the official weights, so neither cached conditioning nor distillation explains it.
why_this_round: Every earlier per-step number either excluded the encoder (round 76 injected precomputed conditioning with text_encoder=False) or was measured on a cold first invocation. The goal asks for a live, comparable measurement, and that number did not exist.

run.model: /tmp/h3_round53_native49_fp16_model, whose symlinks resolve to the official MiniMax-H3 encoders/VAEs plus the official 50-block FP16 transformer
run.engine_kwargs: dtype=half, ulysses_degree=8, ring_degree=1, text_encoder_tp_size=8, vae_parallel_mode=tile, vae_use_tiling=True, vae_patch_parallel_size=8, enable_distributed_layerwise_offload=True, model_loaded={transformer,vae,text_encoder,vae_encoder}=True

request.prompt: a red ball bouncing from left to right on the floor

first_attempt_failed_and_why.error: RuntimeError: RPC call to execute_model timed out.
first_attempt_failed_and_why.root_cause: the client wait bound VLLM_OMNI_ASYNC_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT defaults to 600 s and the first steps (153 s for step 1 while TBE compiled the step's ops) exceeded the per-step wait, so the engine aborted a render that was still progressing
first_attempt_failed_and_why.fix: raised VLLM_OMNI_ASYNC_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT and VLLM_OMNI_DLO_DP_WAVE_TIMEOUT to 3600 s; this is a client wait bound, not a numerical tolerance

co_residency_effect.interpretation: Residency of the text encoder alongside the DiT and VAE more than doubles the DiT per-step cost on this stack. The round-76 figure was measured with text_encoder=False and an injected conditioning payload, so it never contained this cost. This is the missing co-residency term the goal repeatedly flagged as unmeasured.
co_residency_effect.caveat: the two runs differ in more than residency alone (the earlier one also had different step-count bookkeeping in its metrics), so the ratio is a measured indication rather than a clean single-variable experiment; a clean A/B would re-run the same request with text_encoder toggled.

honest_caveats: A2/A3 are the official full-schedule release figures; this stack runs the official 50-block transformer in FP16 on 8x910A under USP8
A2/A3 report T2VA; this request is FL2VA (first/last-frame conditioned), so the workloads are related but not identical
the A2/A3 hardware is not the 910A
these ratios are therefore directional, not an apples-to-apples speed claim

quality_finding.description: frame 48 of the measured request shows a large MNSTXUS wordmark with three triangular marks centred in the frame, a warm glow halo behind it, and ball ghosting on the floor
significance: the run used the LIVE encoder, so cached/injected conditioning is not the cause
the run used the official undistilled weights, so distillation is not the cause
the red ball, grey backdrop and floor render correctly, so the defect is a superimposed learned artefact rather than a wholesale numerical failure
this reproduces the round-76 rejection (unexpected middle logo lettering plus glow and ball ghosting) under conditions that remove both of its remaining explanations

what_this_changes: The stack's real per-step cost at the goal's baseline is ~33.45 s warm with the encoder resident, not 14.657 s. Any speed plan must target the co-resident configuration.

The quality defect is now pinned to the model/stack itself. Chasing encoder precision further cannot fix the logo/ghosting artefact, so the next quality investigation must look at the DiT conditioning consumption, the VAE, and the checkpoint's own behaviour.
The remaining performance gap to official lossless is about 11x per step, which no single kernel recovers; the plan needs the co-residency cost addressed first.
not_claimed: no claim that the 2.28x ratio is a clean single-variable result
